key_insight: lPINN moves most of the learning offline by pretraining a nonlinear neural basis and then solving each new PDE instance with only a fast online linear fit under the physics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This can greatly cut inference cost for forward and inverse PDE problems while preserving accuracy, making it attractive for repeated simulation, parameter estimation, and data-limited scientific workflows.
method: Pretrain continuous, differentiable basis functions from solution ensembles using derivative data or physics residuals.
Freeze the hidden layers for each new case and optimize only the final linear layer online.
Enforce governing-equation residuals plus initial, boundary, regularization, and observation terms.
evidence_signal: Across advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum tests, lPINN reduced solution and parameter errors versus vanilla PINNs and cut online inference time by about 1 to more than 3 orders of magnitude, with strong gains when residual or measurement data were scarce.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of offline training solutions, so poor basis pretraining could limit generalization to new regimes or geometries.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
